decision_summary: Hold: send nothing to anyone. Record the chase and the threat in a case note, and schedule a follow-up for when Harbourline's coverage decision on HM-CA-228904 arrives, due by 2026-10-14. At that point, update the buyer with the real outcome and pass an approval to the seller so the replacement ships the same day.
rationale: The wait test gives (a) no, (b) yes and (c) yes, so the verdict is hold. Harbourline's decision is due by 2026-10-14, and the buyer was told this on 2026-10-07. The desk has no authority to make Harbourline pay early or to refund on the seller's behalf. Chasing Harbourline is pointless because it has said status is not available before that date and the adjuster has confirmed the file is queued. A holding reply would only restate the promise or tempt an ETA or goodwill offer the owners have not given. Timing: from 2026-10-07 to about 2026-10-21, the firing date is 14 days out. A decision by 2026-10-14 followed by same-day shipping still leaves about 7 days before 2026-10-21, so the existing path can still meet her need.
alternatives_rejected: Replying to the buyer with a holding update or a restated date: this is a restated promise and adds nothing (rule 11).
Asking Harbourline to expedite or pay today: the insurer has said when it will decide, and status is unavailable before then.
Refunding the buyer from the desk: outside desk authority (rule 1).
Asking the seller to ship the spare kiln now: the seller has already stated its position (wait for approval), and that is the seller's decision.
Escalating to a human supervisor: a chargeback or review threat is not a safety, fraud or authority issue that needs a human decision.
